observation_summary: The CSS selector parser fails with a SelectorParseException when an attribute regex selector (e.g., [class~=x|y]) is used in combination with other selectors (e.g., 'div table[class~=x|y]').
hypothesis: The TokenQueue parser logic in the Selector class is incorrectly consuming or failing to handle the pipe character '|' within the attribute regex value, causing the parser to misinterpret the remaining query string as an unexpected token.
prediction: The fix will involve updating the TokenQueue or the Selector's attribute parsing logic to correctly handle the pipe character inside attribute regex values, ensuring it is not treated as a delimiter or unexpected token.
experiment_rationale: The failure occurs during parsing of the query string. Since the parser throws an exception when it encounters the pipe character, the logic responsible for tokenizing the attribute selector is likely too restrictive or incorrectly configured for regex values containing special characters.
reasoning_summary: The issue is a failure in the parsing procedure (the algorithm used to tokenize and interpret the CSS selector string). It is not a missing guard (Checking), a wrong value (Assignment), or a design-level capability issue (Function/Class/Object). It is a procedural error in how the selector string is processed, making Algorithm/Method the most appropriate classification.
evidence_used: org.jsoup.select.Selector$SelectorParseException: Could not parse query '=x|y]': unexpected token at '=x|y]'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the parser throws an exception, the root cause is the incorrect implementation of the parsing algorithm for regex attributes, not just a missing validation check.
The issue is internal to the Selector's parsing logic, not a mismatch between two different components or modules.
